findings.text: The diff writes false "gone" lines into eleven unrelated `files.jsonl` indexes (Requirements, the indexing check). The worktree has no copies of gitignored files, so its indexer marked them gone, e.g. `ai/files.jsonl` +`usage.json`/`tasks.json`/`index.jsonl` gone, `ai/sessions/files.jsonl` +`week.json` gone, `ai/whisper/files.jsonl` +`2026-10-09.jsonl` gone. All of these still exist in the main tree (`ls` finds `ai/usage.json`, `ai/tasks.json`, `ai/sessions/week.json`, `ai/whisper/2026-10-09.jsonl`). Commit by path: keep only `ext/Chat/files.jsonl`, `ext/Chat/v1-2/**/files.jsonl` and `core/Session/Chat/files.jsonl`, and drop the rest.

Ask 2's "live Whisper guess" never sits after the cursor. `ChatV1Dot2.entries()` draws only the sentences in `V1Bubbles.events` (ended sentences). The interim guess and the unfinished sentence are not drawn, and the test never feeds one. Either draw the interim words after the ✓, or record in `v1-2/readme.md` Decisions that they are out of scope and why.

`ai/system-map.md:59` is now stale: it says "the Chat tab has three chips". The diff adds a fourth (Chat V1.2, `AISessionDetail.js`), but the map and its versions table (lines 23–42) don't mention V1.2. Add one row and one line.

Ask 3 asked for "dims a little when a sentence is sent, lights green when the assistant has received it". The build has a single stamp (`sent.fast.at`), so the ✓ moves only on receipt and stays dim while later ended sentences wait. This reading is written down in the readme's Decisions with its alternative, so it is fine to land. The owner should still see it when trying it out.

Ask 1 said "a subclass that swaps the source". `ChatV1Dot2 extends JSONL` wraps V1's `chat()` and does not subclass it. That's reasonable because V1 is a function bag, and the readme says so. V1 really is untouched: the diff has no `Chat.js` or `Chat.css` hunk.

In the demo, the unsent sentence "Try a hard refresh." lands in its own owner bubble below the Reply, not after the ✓ in the first bubble (`shots/…-v1-2/400.png`, band 3). This is V1's ordering rule at work, but the cursor then looks as if it ends the conversation's owner text. A fixture with no Reply mid-Prompt would show the ask more clearly.

The walkthrough's shots are under the gitignored `**/shots/` (`.gitignore:210`). The links in `walkthrough.md` will be dead for anyone not on this machine. The walkthrough says so and gives the regenerate command.
New classes `ChatV1Dot2` and `SendCursor` (state: `on`, the cursor's position) have no page showing their live instances (rules.md "Show the class, and its live instances").
The dim ✓ sits at opacity .35 on the pink owner bubble, which makes it hard to see (`shots/…-v1-2/400.png`, "Maybe it is the cache. ✓"). That's intended for "dim", but .5 would still read as a check.

findings.text: Ask 1, "add it to the list so we can try it out": V1.2 is in `ext/Chat/page.js` children and has a chip on the session page, but it is missing from the version dropdown where V1, V2 and V3 sit (`ext/drawer/ChatView.js` `static VERSIONS`, the ✦ sheet and the drawer). That dropdown is the only place with a live composer, so it is the only place the owner can watch the cursor and the live draft (the `chat-live` event) while dictating.

The review shots of `/framework/ext/Chat/v1-2/` (`400.png`, band 3) show the older look: the owner's avatar sits in each pill and the Reply has a grey bubble. The builder's own `shots/v1-2-360.png` shows the Claude-style layout from `bubbles.css`, which the branch contains (`Chat.js:8`). The shot server most likely served stale CSS. Before merging, check the demo page by eye.

The demo fixture still puts the unsent "Try a hard refresh." in its own bubble below the Reply (`400.png`, band 3). V1's rule closes a bubble once a Reply lands, so this is by design and the builder accepted it. Even so, the ✓ looks as though it ends the owner's turn.

"Dims when sent, lit when received" is built as "dim while ended sentences wait". It is a documented decision with the alternative named (v1-2/readme.md, Decisions). Ask 1's "subclass" is a wrap, because V1 is a function bag; that is also documented.
